questions.question: The Narmada River rises in which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amarkantak hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada River** is one of the major rivers in India and is** known as the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• The river rises from the** Amarkantak hills near Anuppur district** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Narmada river is about **1,312 km long** and is the** fifth-largest river in India** in terms of length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada River** flows through three states of India, viz., **Madhya Pradesh, Gujrat and Maharastra,** and **ends at the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea.**
 
• This river** does not form deltas**; instead,** it forms estuaries**.
 
• It is a **west-flowing river**. Other prominent **west-flowing rivers are Tapi, Mahi, Periyar, Vaitarana, Bharatpuzha,** etc. 
 
• It** flows through the Rift Valley.** Other prominent rivers that **flow through the rift valley are Tapi, Son and Mahi**.
 
• The river has several dams, including the **Sardar Sarovar Dam, Indira Sagar Dam**, etc.
 
• Some prominent waterfalls on the river** Dhuandhar, Dugdh Dhara, Kapil Dhara, Sahastra Dhara**, etc. 
 
• **Nasik** is a city in Maharashtra and is known for its religious significance as it is the **source of the Godavari River.**

questions.question: The Code of Criminal Procedure was enacted in year _______ in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1973.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** is a procedural law that **governs the process of investigation** and** trial of criminal cases** in India.
 
• The CrPC was **enacted in 1973** and came **into force on April 1, 1974.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Following the Indian uprising of 1857, the** British** crown assumed control of the country, and **in 1861 the Criminal Procedure Code was passed**.
 
• The legacy of British India lasted until 1973, when the present Code was passed and went into effect on April 1st, 1974.
 
• The **main objective** of the CrPC is **to ensure a fair and just investigation and trial of criminal cases**, while also **protecting the rights of the accused and the victims.**
 
• It offers the tools necessary for conducting criminal investigations, apprehending suspected offenders, gathering evidence, establishing the guilt or innocence of the accused, and determining the appropriate punishment for the guilty.
 
• In addition, it addresses maintaining a spouse, child, and parents as well as preventing offenses and public nuisances.
 
• **The Code of Criminal Procedure** is divided into** 37 chapters** with **484 sections, 2 schedules,** and **56 forms.**
 
• A Bill to replace the CrPC with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was presented in the Lok Sabha on August 11, 2023.

questions.question: In the Tamil region, landless labourers, including slaves, were known as _____ during Sangam age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kadaisiyar and Adimai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slaves and landless labourers **in the Tamil region during the **Sangam era** were referred to as "**kadaisiyar and adimai**."
 
• People who **had to work extremely hard to survive **at the** bottom of the social hierarchy** were referred to as "**kadaisiyar**."
 
• **Slaves** who were **owned by landlords** and compelled to work for them were known as "**adimai**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Sangam Age**, sometimes referred to as the** Tamil Sangam period**, was an important period in South India's history. It is generally believed that the Sangam era occurred **between 300 BCE and 300 CE**.
 
• **Three dynasties—the Chera, Chola, and Pandyas**—ruled the Tamil nation during the Sangam Period. They were **Muvendar**, jointly as well.
 
• For administrative convenience, the **kingdom was split **into the following **divisions: Mandalam (territory), Nadu (province), Ur (town), Perur (large village), and Sirur (small village).**
 
• **More terms used in sangam age**:
 
 
• Karai: Land tax 
 
• Ulgu: Customs duties
 
• Iravu: Forced gift/extra demand 
 
• Irai: Tribute paid by feudatories 
 
• Variyar: Tax collector
 
• Vanigar: Traders and Merchants
 
• Arasar: Ruling Class
 
• **Vellalars**: Dominant Agricultural caste
 
• **Uzhavars**: Middle-class Agricultural caste

questions.question: Who was responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**General Dyer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**, also known as the **Amritsar massacre**, took place on **13 April 1919**.
 
• During the annual** Baishakhi festival** in Amritsar, Punjab, British India, a sizable and nonviolent gathering had convened at the Jallianwala Bagh to express **disapproval of the Rowlatt Act** and the apprehension of pro-independence activists **Saifuddin Kitchlew** and **Satyapal**.
 
• Temporary **Brigadier General Reginald E. H. Dyer** encircled the mass of unarmed civilians and ordered open fire in reaction to their public gathering.
 
• After the incident, **Rabindranath Tagore renounced his 'Knighthood".**
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi **gave up his title of** 'Kaiser-i-Hind'** and **withdrew the Satyagrah against Rowlatt Act.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rowlatt Act**:

 
 
• The Rowlatt Act, also known as the** Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, was enacted by the British government, prompting the Rowlatt Satyagraha. 
 
• On the advice of the **Sir Sidney Rowlatt** who **chaired Sedition Committee**, this act was passed. Despite the Indian members' unanimous opposition, the Imperial Legislative Council rushed this act through **in March 1919.**
 
• It gave the government broad powers to stifle political activity and allowed the** two-year imprisonment of political prisoners without charge or trial.**
 
• Gandhiji demanded that the Rowlatt Act be opposed nationally.

questions.question: ______ is an electronic payment system that enables customers of a bank or other financial institution to conduct a range of financial transactions through the financial institution's website.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Internet banking.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Internet banking** is also known as **online banking or e-banking.**
 
• It **allows customers** to **perform** various financial transactions such as c**hecking account balances, transferring funds, paying bills, and applying for loans **through the bank's website.
 
• Internet banking is a convenient and secure way for customers to manage their finances **without having to visit a bank branch**.
 
• Some of the benefits of internet banking include 24/7 access to account information, faster transactions, and lower fees compared to traditional banking methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interstate banking** refers to the **ability of banks to operate branches in multiple states**. This allows banks to expand their reach and offer their services to customers in different regions.
 
• A s**ingle-entry system** is an **accounting method** where each **financial transaction is recorded only once**, either as a debit or a credit. This method is **simpler than double-entry** accounting and is often used by small businesses.
 
• **Inter-corporate banking** refers to** financial transactions between two or more corporations**. This can include loans, investments, and other financial services.

questions.question: Manufacturing sectors are considered as the _____ of general and economic development.
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**backbone.**__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A nation's manufacturing sectors are essential to its economic development and growth.**
 
• It is a part of **secondary sector.**
 
• A **nation's GDP is greatly increased by the manufacturing sector**, which also generates employment opportunities for the populace.
 
• By supplying raw materials and completed goods, the manufacturing sector also contributes to the expansion of other industries like transportation, agriculture, and services.
 
• **Innovation and technical breakthroughs are also facilitated by the manufacturing sector**, which further propels economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector**

 
 
• Activities in the primary sector of the economy** involve the direct use of natural resources**. Some examples of this industry are agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry, dairy, and so on.
 
• It is thus named because it serves as the foundation for all other goods. It is **also known as the "agriculture and allied sector" **because the majority of the natural products we use come from **forestry, fishery, dairy, and agriculture.**
 
• Because primary activities require working outside, those who engage in them are referred to as **red-collar workers**.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector**
 
 
• It encompasses the sectors in which **natural resources generated in the primary sector are used to create final goods. **This sector includes operations such as **sugar cane production, cotton fabric production, and industrial production.**
 
• Therefore, it is the sector of an economy that produces goods rather than raw materials.
 
• This sector is **also known as the industrial sector **because it is connected to several industries.
 
• **Blue collar workers** are those who perform auxiliary tasks.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector/Service Sector**
 
 
• The primary and secondary sectors benefit from the activity of this sector. Economic activity in the tertiary sector **assists or supports production rather than producing commodities on its own**.
 
• The industry includes things like **banking, insurance, finance, and truck or train-borne freight.** It adds value to a product in the same way as the secondary sector.
 
• **White collar jobs** are those in this industry.​

questions.question: Cell is the ______ living part of an organism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**smallest.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **cell is the smallest living part of an organism.** It is the basic unit of life and the building block of all living organisms.
 
• The word "cell" comes from the** Latin word "cellula",** which means **"small room"**.
 
• Cells are responsible for carrying out all the functions necessary for an organism to survive and grow, such as obtaining nutrients, eliminating waste, and reproducing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Robert Hooke** makes the **discovery of the cell in 1665**.
 
• **Prokaryotic** and** eukaryotic **cells are the two different **types of cells**.
 
 
• A **prokaryotic cell's nucleus is absent**. As an alternative, certain prokaryotes, like bacteria, have a section of their cells where the genetic material is allowed to float freely. The nucleoid is the term for this area. Each of them is a **single-celled microbe**. **Bacteria, cyanobacteria, and archaea** are among examples.
 
• Cells classified as **eukaryotic have a genuine nucleus**. This large category includes animals, plants, fungus, and protozoa. The monitoring of the movement of nutrients and electrolytes into and out of cells is the responsibility of the plasma membrane. It is also in charge of cell-to-cell transmission.
 
 
 
• **Cell organelles are**:
 
 
• **Nucleolus:** The nucleolus is where ribosome synthesis takes place. Moreover, it has a role in regulating both cellular proliferation and activity.
 
• **Nuclear Membrane:** By creating a barrier between the nucleus and other cell organelles, the nuclear membrane shields the nucleus from harm.
 
• **Golgi bodies:** Because golgi bodies are crucial in the movement of materials within cells, they are referred to as the post office of the cell.
 
• **Mitochondria:** It is said that the mitochondrion is "the powerhouse of the cell." It generates ATP, the energy currency of the cell, which is why it gets its name.
 
• **Lysosomes:** Lysosomes aid in cell renewal and provide protection to the cell by swallowing foreign objects that enter it. As a result, they are referred to as the suicide bags of the cell.
 
• **Chloroplast: **The principal organelles involved in photosynthesis are chloroplasts. Chlorophyll is a pigment found in it.

questions.question: What does Sub-Section (g) of the list of Fundamental Duties deal with?

options.text: Protect and improve the natural environment
Preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protect and improve the natural environment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part IV A **of the Indian Constitution contains **Article 51A,** which deals with the **Fundamental Duties**.
 
• The **Soviet Constitution (USSR)** is where the** idea of fundamental duties originated**.
 
• Fundamental Duties were** recommended** in **1976** by the **Swaran Singh Committee.**
 
• Ten Fundamental Duties were **added** to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• **Article 51A(g): Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added ten fundamental duties.
 
• The** 86th Amendment** to the Constitution was passed in **2002**, **adding the eleventh fundamental duty**.
 
• **The list of Fundamental Duties as mentioned in the Article 51A:**

5.

6.

10.

11.

 
 
 
Provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

• **Green Revolution** was a significant agricultural transformation that took place in India **during the 1960s and 1970s**.
 
• The **aim of this revolution** was to **increase the productivity of agricultural crops**, particularly **wheat and rice,** through the use of **high-yielding varieties, modern farming techniques, and better irrigation facilities.**
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan**, the renowned agricultural scientist, is referred to as the **"Father of the Green Revolution."**
 
• The Green Revolution played a crucial role in addressing India's food security concerns by **increasing food production and reducing the country's dependence on food imports.**

questions.question: IPR-1956 laid the foundation of the ______ Five-Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Industrial Policy of 1956

 
 
• Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 (IPR 1956) is a resolution adopted by the Indian Parliament in April 1956.
 
• It was the first comprehensive statement on the industrial development of India. 
 
• It was regarded as the “Economic Constitution of India” or “The Bible of State Capitalism”.
 
• The government revised its first Industrial Policy (i.e.the policy of 1948) through the Industrial Policy of 1956.
 
• The 1956 Policy empha­sised the need to expand the public sector, to build up a large and growing coop­erative sector and to encourage the separation of ownership and management in private in­dustries and, above all, prevent the rise of pri­vate monopolies.
 
• It provided the basic framework for the government’s policy regarding in­dustries till June 1991.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Planning Commission was established in 1950 to formulate and implement five-year plans for economic development in India.
 
• **The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)** aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.7% per annum and focused on the development of agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.
 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)** was based on the Mahalanobis model of economic development and aimed to achieve a growth rate of 4.5% per annum. It focused on heavy industries, particularly steel, and aimed to reduce the dependence on imports.
 
• **The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985)** aimed to achieve a growth rate of 5.2% per annum and focused on poverty alleviation, employment generation, and rural development.
 
• **The Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002-2007)** aimed to achieve a growth rate of 8% per annum and focused on human development, infrastructure development, and regional development.
